# `silk/bench/units`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Text for the quantities of a benchmark report: durations, memory sizes, and ratios.

## When to use
Use [`Units`](#Units) in a renderer of your own, so its numbers read like those of the built-in
reports: `12.3 ms`, `4.20 MiB`, `0.49x`.

## Details
A duration is given in nanoseconds and written with three significant digits in the largest
unit that keeps it at 1 or more: `ns`, `µs`, `ms`, or `s`. A [`Scale`](#Scale) fixes the unit, so the
numbers of one column share it and line up. Memory is given in bytes and written in binary
units: `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB`.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.units { Units }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.text.string { String }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let time = run Units.duration(12345678.0)
  let size = run Units.memory(4404019.0)
  if String.view(&time) == "12.3 ms" && String.view(&size) == "4.20 MiB" {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}

effect fn failed(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `Units` with `import silk.bench.units { Units }`.

<a id="Units.impl.scale"></a>

### Associated function `scale`

```silk
pub fn scale(nanoseconds: f64) -> Scale
```

Returns the largest unit in which `nanoseconds` is 1 or more, or `ns` for less than 1 µs.

<a id="Units.impl.kind"></a>

### Associated function `kind`

```silk
pub fn kind(unit: string) -> string<'static>
```

Returns the kind of the unit `unit`, which decides how its values are scaled: `ns` for a
time in nanoseconds, `B` for bytes, and nothing for any other unit.

#### Details
What counts is the text before the first `/`, after a qualifier that ends with `-`. So
`ns/op`, `user-ns/op` and `ns` are times, and `B/op` and `peak-B` are bytes.

<a id="Units.impl.higher"></a>

### Associated function `higher`

```silk
pub fn higher(unit: string) -> bool
```

Returns whether a larger value of the unit `unit` is better: a unit that ends with `/s`
or `/sec`, such as `req/s` or `MB/s`. For every other unit, smaller is better.

<a id="Units.impl.measure"></a>

### Associated function `measure`

```silk
pub fn measure(value: f64, unit: string) -> Scale
```

Returns the scale in which `value` of the unit `unit` reads best: the largest one in which
it is 1 or more.

<a id="Units.impl.named"></a>

### Associated function `named`

```silk
pub fn named<'unit>(scale: Scale, unit: string<'unit>) -> string<'unit>
```

Returns the name that follows the numbers of a column in `scale`: the scale's own name for
a time or memory, and `unit` as it is for any other unit.

<a id="Units.impl.quantity"></a>

### Associated function `quantity`

```silk
pub effect fn quantity(value: f64, unit: string) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns `value` of the unit `unit` as text with its unit, such as `12.3 ms`, `4.20 MiB` or
`74.2k req/s`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="Units.impl.appendFixed"></a>

### Associated function `appendFixed`

```silk
pub effect fn appendFixed(text: &mut String, value: f64, decimals: usize) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends `value` to `text` with `decimals` digits after the point, rounded half away from
zero. A value that is not finite is written as `-`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow `text`.

<a id="Units.impl.appendSignificant"></a>

### Associated function `appendSignificant`

```silk
pub effect fn appendSignificant(text: &mut String, value: f64) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends `value` to `text` with three significant digits: `1.23`, `12.3`, or `123`. Values
of 1000 or more keep all their whole digits.
